nodes.label: The MiddleEast market shows the highest average return rate at 0.4312 while simu…
nodes.summary:
The MiddleEast market shows the highest average return rate at 0.4312 while simultaneously delivering the highest average revenue per customer at €1,664.25, highlighting elevated post‑purchase returns despite strong spend [1]. This juxtaposition raises profitability concerns even as revenue remains robust.

Mytheresa records the highest overall return rate at 0.459024, yet its customer satisfaction score (4.05) lags slightly behind NET‑A‑PORTER’s 4.11, which enjoys a lower return rate (0.443489) [2]. The gap suggests that higher returns may be eroding brand perception despite comparable spend levels.

Supply‑side concentration is evident: Italy supplies 38.57% of LuxExperience’s catalog (27 brands), far outpacing France’s 24.29% share [3], while THE OUTNET leads in VIP customer concentration with a tier_customer_rate of 0.100506, exceeding Mytheresa and NET‑A‑PORTER [4]. Such concentrations amplify exposure to regional or platform‑specific shocks.

data.sql: WITH payment_by_order AS (SELECT p.order_id, (EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM luxexperience.order_items AS oi_returned WHERE oi_returned.order_id = p.order_id AND oi_returned.returned = TRUE) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM luxexperience.order_items AS oi_not_returned WHERE oi_not_returned.order_id = p.order_id AND oi_not_returned.returned = FALSE)) AS segment, SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'refunded' THEN p.amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS payment_refund_eur, COUNT(*) AS payment_record_n FROM luxexperience.payments AS p GROUP BY 1, 2), returns_by_order AS (SELECT r.order_id, SUM(r.refund_eur) AS returns_refund_eur FROM luxexperience.returns AS r WHERE NOT r.refund_eur IS NULL GROUP BY 1), order_metrics AS (SELECT payment_by_order.segment, payment_by_order.payment_refund_eur, COALESCE(returns_by_order.returns_refund_eur, 0) AS returns_refund_eur, payment_by_order.payment_record_n FROM payment_by_order LEFT JOIN returns_by_order ON payment_by_order.order_id = returns_by_order.order_id), overall_gap AS (SELECT ((SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'refunded' THEN p.amount_eur ELSE 0 END) FROM luxexperience.payments AS p) - (SELECT SUM(r.refund_eur) FROM luxexperience.returns AS r WHERE NOT r.refund_eur IS NULL)) AS refund_reporting_gap_eur) SELECT order_metrics.segment, SUM(order_metrics.payment_refund_eur) AS metric_total, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(SUM(order_metrics.payment_refund_eur) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS avg_per_record, SUM(order_metrics.returns_refund_eur) AS returns_reported_refunds_eur, SUM(order_metrics.payment_refund_eur) - SUM(order_metrics.returns_refund_eur) AS partial_return_explained_gap_eur, ROUND(100.0 * (SUM(order_metrics.payment_refund_eur) - SUM(order_metrics.returns_refund_eur)) / NULLIF(overall_gap.refund_reporting_gap_eur, 0), 1) AS partial_return_gap_explained_pct FROM order_metrics CROSS JOIN overall_gap GROUP BY 1, overall_gap.refund_reporting_gap_eur ORDER BY 1

data.sql: WITH shipment_base AS (SELECT s.origin_country || ' → ' || s.destination_country AS route, COALESCE(s.shipping_cost_eur, 0) AS shipping_cost_eur, COALESCE(o.shipping_fee_eur, 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY s.order_id), 0) AS allocated_shipping_fee_eur FROM luxexperience.shipments AS s JOIN luxexperience.orders AS o ON o.order_id = s.order_id), dimension_metrics AS (SELECT route, SUM(shipping_cost_eur) - SUM(allocated_shipping_fee_eur) AS metric_total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM shipment_base GROUP BY route) SELECT route, metric_total, n, ROUND(metric_total / NULLIF(n, 0), 2) AS avg_per_record, ROUND(100.0 * metric_total / NULLIF(SUM(metric_total) OVER (), 0), 1) AS pct_of_total FROM dimension_metrics ORDER BY metric_total ASC LIMIT 15

data.sql: WITH logistics_dedup AS (SELECT return_id, condition, carrier, refund_method, restocked, refund_completed_date FROM (SELECT rl.return_id, rl.condition, rl.carrier, rl.refund_method, rl.restocked, rl.refund_completed_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rl.return_id ORDER BY rl.return_logistics_id) AS rn FROM luxexperience.return_logistics AS rl) AS ranked_logistics WHERE rn = 1) SELECT r.category AS category, SUM(r.refund_eur) AS metric_total, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(SUM(r.refund_eur) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS avg_per_record, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(r.refund_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(SUM(r.refund_eur)) OVER (), 0), 1) AS pct_of_total FROM luxexperience.returns AS r JOIN logistics_dedup AS rl ON rl.return_id = r.return_id JOIN luxexperience.order_items AS oi ON oi.order_item_id = r.order_item_id WHERE NOT r.refund_eur IS NULL AND NOT rl.refund_completed_date IS NULL AND rl.restocked = FALSE GROUP BY r.category ORDER BY metric_total DESC LIMIT 15

data.sql: WITH delivery_by_destination AS (/* Avoid shipment fan-out: one avg delivery per order_id, then aggregate by destination */ WITH per_order AS (SELECT o.ship_country, o.ship_region, s.order_id, AVG(s.delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days FROM luxexperience.shipments AS s JOIN luxexperience.orders AS o ON o.order_id = s.order_id WHERE NOT s.delivery_days IS NULL GROUP BY 1, 2, 3) SELECT ship_country, ship_region, AVG(avg_delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days FROM per_order GROUP BY 1, 2), return_rate_by_destination AS (SELECT o.ship_country, o.ship_region, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN o.order_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN o.order_id END), 0) AS return_rate FROM luxexperience.orders AS o GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT d.ship_country, d.ship_region, d.avg_delivery_days, r.return_rate FROM delivery_by_destination AS d LEFT JOIN return_rate_by_destination AS r ON r.ship_country = d.ship_country AND r.ship_region = d.ship_region ORDER BY d.avg_delivery_days DESC, r.return_rate DESC LIMIT 15

data.sql: WITH refunds_by_returned_order AS (SELECT o.fiscal_year, r.order_id, SUM(r.refund_eur) AS refund_eur FROM luxexperience.returns AS r JOIN luxexperience.orders AS o ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.status = 'returned' GROUP BY 1, 2), returned_orders_gmv AS (SELECT o.fiscal_year, o.order_id, o.gmv_eur FROM luxexperience.orders AS o WHERE o.status = 'returned') SELECT g.fiscal_year, SUM(COALESCE(rb.refund_eur, 0)) AS total_refunds_eur, SUM(g.gmv_eur) AS total_gmv_eur, SUM(COALESCE(rb.refund_eur, 0)) / NULLIF(SUM(g.gmv_eur), 0) AS refund_coverage_pct FROM returned_orders_gmv AS g LEFT JOIN refunds_by_returned_order AS rb ON rb.fiscal_year = g.fiscal_year AND rb.order_id = g.order_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

nodes.label: Refund coverage burden (refund_eur ÷ orders.gmv_eur) is slightly declining overa…
nodes.summary: Refund coverage burden (refund_eur ÷ orders.gmv_eur) is slightly declining overall: from 0.700 in 2021 to about 0.689 in 2024 (then ~0.692 in 2025), so refunds are not rising faster than GMV of affected orders.

data.sql: WITH rev AS (SELECT c.region, SUM(o.gmv_eur) AS total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers, SUM(o.gmv_eur) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id), 0) AS avg_revenue_per_customer FROM luxexperience.orders AS o JOIN luxexperience.customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.region), ret AS (SELECT c.region, COUNT(DISTINCT r.order_id) AS refunded_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS eligible_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT r.order_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 0) AS return_rate FROM luxexperience.orders AS o JOIN luxexperience.customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id LEFT JOIN luxexperience.returns AS r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.status IN ('shipped', 'returned') GROUP BY c.region) SELECT r.region, r.avg_revenue_per_customer, rt.return_rate FROM rev AS r JOIN ret AS rt ON r.region = rt.region ORDER BY r.region

data.sql: WITH mr_porter_totals AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS total_customers, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.is_top_customer THEN c.customer_id END) AS total_top_customers FROM luxexperience.customers AS c WHERE c.platform = 'MR PORTER'), mr_porter_us AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.region = 'US' THEN c.customer_id END) AS customers_in_us, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.region = 'US' AND c.is_top_customer THEN c.customer_id END) AS top_customers_in_us FROM luxexperience.customers AS c WHERE c.platform = 'MR PORTER'), computed AS (SELECT u.top_customers_in_us, t.total_top_customers, u.customers_in_us, t.total_customers, u.top_customers_in_us / NULLIF(t.total_top_customers, 0) AS top_customers_us_share, u.customers_in_us / NULLIF(t.total_customers, 0) AS customers_us_share FROM mr_porter_us AS u CROSS JOIN mr_porter_totals AS t) SELECT top_customers_us_share, customers_us_share, top_customers_in_us, total_top_customers, customers_in_us, total_customers FROM computed

nodes.summary: Combining the MR PORTER platform-level concentration with the US regional concentration shows that the US segment’s top-customer count (50) within the US total customers (1248) corresponds to an overall concentration level of 0.387597 for MR PORTER.

data.sql: WITH top_customer_metric AS (SELECT c.platform, COUNT(*) AS total_customers, SUM(CASE WHEN c.is_top_customer THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS top_customers, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN c.is_top_customer THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS top_customer_rate FROM luxexperience.customers AS c GROUP BY c.platform), vip_tier_metric AS (SELECT c.platform, COUNT(*) AS total_customers, SUM(CASE WHEN c.tier = 'VIP' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS vip_customers, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN c.tier = 'VIP' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS tier_customer_rate FROM luxexperience.customers AS c GROUP BY c.platform), metrics AS (SELECT tcm.platform, tcm.top_customer_rate, vtm.tier_customer_rate, ABS(tcm.top_customer_rate - vtm.tier_customer_rate) AS abs_discrepancy FROM top_customer_metric AS tcm JOIN vip_tier_metric AS vtm ON tcm.platform = vtm.platform) SELECT platform, top_customer_rate, tier_customer_rate, abs_discrepancy FROM metrics ORDER BY abs_discrepancy DESC LIMIT 1
